h1: Paradise Hotel Udonthani — a city hotel on Posri Road that sells itself on the airport-close location and good value
intro: If you fly into Udon Thani in the evening and just want to reach your hotel quickly without a long drive, Paradise Hotel Udonthani is an option a lot of people end up considering · it's a 3-star city hotel on Posri Road in Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, only about 10–15 min by car from Udon Thani Airport and just around 1.1 km from the train station · it's about a 10-min walk to Central Plaza Udon Thani · there's an outdoor pool with a kids' pool, a gym, a pool-view restaurant, and free parking · what people talk about most is the affordable price and the well-kept pool and garden · rooms start at about THB 1,600/night, with average scores in the rough 7–8.x range across several real booking platforms.

body.html: Who Paradise Hotel Udonthani is for — to put it as simply as possible, Paradise Hotel Udonthani is a city hotel for people who want a central Udon location at a budget-friendly price while still getting a pool and free parking · it isn't a 4–5 star hotel selling luxury, and it isn't a brand-new boutique trading on style · instead it's a 3-star hotel that's been part of Udon for a long time, last given a major renovation back in 2011, on Posri Road in Mak Khaeng, Mueang district, a neighbourhood that's easy to get in and out of both the town centre and the airport · from real reviews across several platforms, the people it suits best are travellers who fly into Udon and want to reach their hotel fast, self-drivers who want free and roomy parking, families with kids because there's a separate kids' pool, and budget-minded travellers who weigh value over luxury · another group that says it works well are people here on business or stopping one night before continuing to Nong Khai or crossing over to Vientiane · those after a brand-new hotel, heavily designed rooms, or five-star service may need to adjust expectations or look at other options in town · in short, this is a hotel that plays on "good value and convenient" rather than "luxurious."

Location and getting around — this is Paradise Hotel's main selling point · the hotel sits at 44/29 Posri Road in Mak Khaeng, Mueang district, right in a residential and shopping part of Udon Thani · the clear advantage is that it's only about 5–6 km, or roughly 10–15 min by car, from Udon Thani Airport (UTH), so people flying in reach their hotel quickly without a long drive · it's also just about 1.1 km from Udon Thani train station and only a few minutes' drive from the bus terminal, making it a great fit for anyone travelling by train or coach · on the shopping and dining side, it's about a 10-min walk to Central Plaza Udon Thani, and a short drive on to UD Town, the popular night market · around the hotel there's also Wat Phothisomphon and a monument within walking distance · one small note: Posri Road is a main road with fairly heavy traffic at rush hour, so rooms facing the street may catch some traffic noise, and the area is a real working city, not a quiet tourist quarter — so anyone wanting a quiet resort vibe may find this isn't the answer · but for people who care about easy access to the city and the airport, this location does well for the price.

"We picked this place because it's close to the airport and the train station — get off the plane, short ride, and you're there · the parking is spacious, the pool is clean, the garden is well kept, and the staff are friendly. Getting a room at this price in town is really good value."

Room types and decor — Paradise Hotel has around 100 rooms across several tiers to suit your budget and group size · it starts with Standard and Superior rooms of about 21 sqm, the entry rooms for a couple or solo traveller · stepping up to Deluxe and Grand Deluxe at about 24.5–28 sqm, which are larger and some come with a small balcony overlooking the pool · for families there are Family Rooms and Family Suites of about 35 sqm plus a Junior Suite of around 36 sqm · the largest is the Royal Suite at about 58 sqm, with a split bathroom that has both a tub and a shower · every room has air conditioning, a minibar, cable TV, a hot-and-cold shower, and free Wi-Fi around the clock · the decor is a simple, warm-toned city-hotel style, nothing flashy like a new boutique, but comfortable to use · real reviews are fairly split: many say the rooms are nicer than expected for the price, with a small balcony over the tidy garden, but some grumble that the Deluxe room looks bigger online than in person, and that some rooms' furniture is starting to show its age along with the building · the thing to watch is cleanliness in some rooms, with reviews mentioning dust or bathrooms that aren't kept up consistently — something worth checking at check-in, and you can ask to switch rooms if it's not okay.

Facilities, pool and spa — the most talked-about highlight at Paradise Hotel is the well-kept outdoor pool with a garden, plus a separate kids' pool that puts families with little ones more at ease · many reviews agree the pool is clean, the water is clear, and the pool area and surrounding garden feel leafier than expected for a hotel at this price · the pool is open from daytime into the evening · besides the pool there's a gym open from morning to evening for anyone who wants to work out, and a massage/spa room to unwind after travelling · for extras there's spacious free parking, a point self-drivers praise often, since finding parking in central Udon isn't always easy · there's also a shuttle service, meeting rooms and event space for seminars or banquets, a bar/lounge, laundry service, and a 24-hour front desk · to be honest, the pool and gym are typical of a city hotel, not big or luxurious like a resort, but in terms of how complete and well-maintained they are, they do well for the price level.

Food and bar — the hotel has a pool-view restaurant (Pool View Restaurant) that serves meals and is where guests have breakfast · breakfast is where reviews vary quite a bit — some say the buffet is decent, with eggs cooked to order and several ready-to-serve dishes · while others grumble that breakfast is rather plain, mostly Asian dishes, and service can be slow when it's busy · one thing to know is that at certain times or on certain packages the room rate may not include breakfast, so check the conditions carefully when booking to see whether your chosen package includes it · beyond the main restaurant there's a bar/lounge for an evening drink · an upside of the location is that if you don't want to eat in the hotel every meal, it's easy to find food around town — Isan restaurants, rice-porridge spots, and a night market all a short drive away · overall, food at Paradise Hotel is a serviceable add-on, not a reason to come and eat in the hotel specifically; it's better suited to using the hotel as a base and going out to eat.

Service — service at Paradise Hotel gets two-sided reviews, as you'd expect from a budget city hotel · on the plus side, many praise the reception staff as friendly, helpful, polite, and good at giving travel tips or calling a car · the 24-hour front desk makes it easy for people arriving late or flying in at night to check in · on the flip side, some reviews say certain staff or certain times of day aren't as cheerful or attentive across the board, and the response on some things can be slow when it's busy · to be straight about it, this is common at hotels of this level, and overall most guests still feel the service is acceptable and good value for the price · if you have an issue with the room or cleanliness, telling staff directly at check-in usually gets it sorted faster.

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulled together from Trip.com, Booking.com, Hotels.com and TripAdvisor, the picture lines up fairly consistently · on the praise side: a location near the airport and train station with easy access in and out of town, free and roomy parking, a clean pool and well-kept garden, good value for a room in town, and some rooms nicer than expected at this price · on the gripes side: the thing brought up most often is the air conditioning in some rooms not getting cold enough or not cooling well, especially in the hot season · next is inconsistent cleanliness in some rooms, with reviews mentioning dust or a smell in some bathrooms, furniture and the building starting to age since the major renovation back in 2011, the online Deluxe room photos looking bigger than reality, and breakfast and service being just okay at times · most of these gripes are things you can manage by choosing your room, checking it at check-in, and setting expectations to match the price level, rather than big problems that keep people from coming back.

"The pool and garden are nicer than the price suggests, and parking is very easy · the only gripe was the room AC not getting cold enough during the day — I told the staff and they came to adjust it. Next time I'll ask for a freshly cleaned room that doesn't face the street."

Price and value compared — the starting price for a Standard room is around THB 1,600/night at the hotel's rate, though some platforms and promotional periods may show it lower · Deluxe and Grand Deluxe rooms run roughly THB 2,000–2,500, while family rooms and suites step up to about THB 3,500–4,500 depending on size and season · compared with a downtown 4-star hotel like Centara Udon, which starts at around THB 1,200 and up but has nicer rooms and common areas, Paradise Hotel sells a different angle — the pool and garden, spacious free parking, and a location near the airport and train station — at a price still in the budget bracket · so the value comes down to what you weigh — if you want to walk to a mall and have plush common areas, a mall-side hotel may be better value, but if you prioritise parking, a pool, a garden, and easy access to the airport and train station, Paradise Hotel offers value in its own way · always compare prices across a few platforms before booking, since rates at this level move quite a bit with season and promotions.

Good to know before booking — a few things make for a smoother stay · one, if you're sensitive to noise or want quiet, ask for a room that doesn't face Posri Road and is on the inner side overlooking the pool, since this road is busy at rush hour · two, the AC is a common complaint, so test it at check-in and ask to change rooms right away if it doesn't cool well · three, check the breakfast terms carefully to see whether your booked package includes breakfast, as some rates don't · four, if you're driving, the free parking here is a strong point — make the most of it · five, the cool season (December–February) is Isan's high season, when prices climb and rooms fill fast, so book ahead and pick free cancellation if your plans aren't set · six, check the room's condition and cleanliness on arrival, and if anything's not okay, tell staff right away — it usually gets handled faster than waiting until checkout.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Paradise Hotel Udonthani is the best fit for people who want budget-friendly accommodation in Udon, near the airport and train station, with a pool and free parking · its strengths are an easy-access location, a well-kept pool and garden, and an affordable price, making it a good-value pick for budget travellers, self-drivers, and families who want a kids' pool · the trade-offs you have to accept are the AC in some rooms, inconsistent cleanliness, and a building and furniture that are starting to show their age, since the major renovation dates back to 2011 · if you're after a brand-new hotel, heavily designed rooms, or four-to-five-star service, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a higher-tier city hotel instead · but for a trip focused on value, easy travel, and having a pool and parking ready — Paradise Hotel Udonthani does its job well for the price, as long as you choose your room wisely and set expectations right.

honestSummary: Paradise Hotel Udonthani sells itself on a location near the airport and train station, a well-kept pool and garden, free parking, and good value — a fit for budget travellers, self-drivers, and families who want a kids' pool · the trade-offs are AC in some rooms not getting cold enough, inconsistent cleanliness, and a building that's starting to age since the major renovation back in 2011.
honestChecks: If you want a brand-new hotel or 4–5 star service — this is a 3-star city hotel renovated back in 2011, and some parts are starting to age → look at a higher-tier city hotel if you prioritise luxury and new rooms.

If you're sensitive to noise and want quiet — Posri Road is busy at rush hour and street-facing rooms catch traffic noise → ask for an inner-side room overlooking the pool that doesn't face the street, right from booking.

If you prioritise a location near the airport and free parking — this is the hotel's strong point: close to the airport and train station, with roomy parking → test the AC and check room cleanliness at check-in, and ask to switch right away if it's not okay.

faq.q: Where is Paradise Hotel Udonthani, and how do you get there?
faq.a: The hotel sits at 44/29 Posri Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang, Udon Thani 41000, right in the city area · it's about 5–6 km, or 10–15 min by car, from Udon Thani Airport (UTH) and just about 1.1 km from Udon's train station · it's around a 10-min walk to Central Plaza Udon Thani · there's spacious free parking on site, great for self-drivers or anyone renting a car to tour Udon–Nong Khai.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Paradise Hotel Udonthani, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 1,600/night for a Standard room of around 21 sqm · there are Deluxe and Grand Deluxe rooms at about THB 2,000–2,500 · Family Rooms and suites at about THB 3,500–4,500, up to a Royal Suite of around 58 sqm · prices depend on the season and promotions, climbing in the cool season (Dec–Feb) — compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Paradise Hotel Udonthani have a pool and a gym?
faq.a: Yes · an outdoor pool with a separate kids' pool and a garden that reviews praise as well kept and nicer than the price suggests · there's a gym open from morning to evening, and a massage/spa room to unwind · plus a pool-view restaurant, bar/lounge, meeting rooms, and free parking.

faq.q: What are the rooms at Paradise Hotel Udonthani like — are they clean?
faq.a: Entry rooms are around 21 sqm, decorated in simple warm tones, with AC, a minibar, cable TV, a hot-and-cold shower, and free Wi-Fi · many reviews say some rooms are nicer than expected at this price · the note is that cleanliness in some rooms is inconsistent, with reviews mentioning dust or a bathroom smell, and the AC in some rooms not getting cold enough — check the room at check-in and ask to switch if it's not okay.

faq.q: Who is Paradise Hotel Udonthani best suited to?
faq.a: It's a great fit for budget travellers, self-drivers, and families who want a kids' pool for the children · its strengths are a location near the airport and train station, spacious free parking, and a well-kept pool and garden · it suits people stopping one night before continuing to Nong Khai or crossing over to Vientiane · if you prioritise a new, heavily designed hotel or 4–5 star service, you may want to look at other options in town.

faq.q: Anything to know before booking Paradise Hotel Udonthani?
faq.a: The most common complaints are the AC in some rooms not getting cold enough and inconsistent cleanliness in some rooms · test the AC and check the room's condition at check-in, and ask to switch right away if it's not okay · check carefully whether your booked package includes breakfast, as some rates don't · if you're sensitive to noise, ask for an inner-side room that doesn't face Posri Road · rooms fill fast in the cool season, so book ahead and pick free cancellation.
